headline: Maui County Council Meeting

meeting.voteItem: Motion to discharge the Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee from Resolution 26-147
meeting.summary: The Council advanced water wells for Hawaiian Homelands, sent a Seabury Hall request to the Planning Commission, and backed Kauaʻi hurricane aid.
meeting.recap: One testifier opposed any land zoning changes, saying the lands are royal patented.[[0:15:00]] The Council approved settling a lawsuit against the County with eight ayes and one abstention.[[0:21:38]] A committee report advanced a bill for three water wells on Hawaiian Homelands land.[[0:25:16]] The Council approved the water wells report nine to zero.[[0:31:33]] Committee report 2668 was held because the member leading it had to leave.[[0:32:07]] Seabury Hall plans to move its offices into the head of school house for safety.[[0:44:21]] The bill to help the County of Kauaʻi passed with eight ayes and zero noes.[[1:03:27]] A bill would make developers repay fee waivers when affordable homes sell in higher price tiers.[[1:14:49]] Bills 163 and 164 passed nine to zero.[[1:20:38]] An early flood warning system bill with the Department of the Army passed with eight ayes.[[1:22:08]]
decided: A vote was called on removing the item from committee so the Council could act today, but the result is not heard in the recording.
The Council adopted the resolution to settle a lawsuit against the County.
The bill was moved on first reading, but no vote is in the recording.
A vote was taken on re-funding $3 million for countywide water upgrades, but the count is cut off in the recording.
The fee waiver repayment bill was moved on first reading, but no vote is in the recording.
meeting.next: Committee report 2668 is still to be taken up when the member leading it returns. The vice chair agreed to discuss the sister city topic further in the vice chair's committee.

moments.q: Roll call on the lawsuit settlement

issues.oneLine: The Council advanced a bill for three water wells on Hawaiian Homelands land.
issues.brief: Bill 128 would re-fund $3 million for countywide water upgrades after last year's money lapsed.[[#1]] Bill 129 would allow a loan from the state's Drinking Water State Revolving Fund for water supply projects.[[#2]]
